t: This place is called Pindar, and it takes its name from the ancient Greek poet Pindar. He was a lyric poet from Thebes in the fifth century BC, and of the nine canonical lyric poets of ancient Greece, his work is the best preserved. The Roman teacher Quintilian called him by far the greatest of the nine, praising his inspired magnificence and rolling flood of eloquence. His poems can also seem difficult and even peculiar. That's all the material says about this spot, so the name is the main thing to take with you.
